selected.description: Functional programming language for signal processing and sound synthesis
selected.content_summary: A real Daisy/Hothouse Makefile and audio callback architecture accompany the compiler. The JUCE architecture now initializes effect static tables before instance constants.
selected.portability_summary: Generate a small kernel through the existing Daisy architecture. Keep host adapters and compiler/runtime allocation off the MCU audio callback.
selected.reuse_idea: Use the repaired host initialization path for reference renders, then compare a generated delay on Daisy at the same sample rate.
selected.meaningful_repeat_evidence: 04b121fe initializes effect::classInit for POLY2 effects before instance constants, correcting generated plugin initialization rather than just updating a version.

selected.description: Destroy FX is a music software project of Sophia Poirier and Tom Murphy 7.  Mostly we make audio effect plugins that destroy your sound.  Supported plugin APIs include Audio Unit and VST.  Includes the DfxPlugin and DFX GUI frameworks.
selected.content_summary: iirfilter.cpp implements coefficient calculation and filter paths; firfilter.cpp implements odd-tap ideal low-pass coefficients and window functions.
selected.portability_summary: Extract individual filters and replace framework helpers; review double-precision and C++ library costs on Cortex-M7. The full plug-in framework remains host software.
selected.reuse_idea: Compare the FIR coefficient generator against a host impulse response before translating its bounded tap loop to CMSIS-DSP.
selected.license_note: Inspected filter source headers say GPL-2.0-or-later. The separate BSD text does not establish that these filters are BSD licensed.

selected.description: A standalone app and DAW plugin (AAX / VST3 / AU) that emulates classic hardware synthesizers, samplers, and keyboards by running their original firmware on cycle-accurate CPU and DSP emulators.
selected.content_summary: CA-72 oscillator and nonlinear filter models are real C++ implementations; synth.cpp contains the worker/block deadline policy.
selected.portability_summary: Treat a single oscillator/filter model as a reference. Double-precision nonlinear solves and desktop worker threads require substantial simplification and measured MCU budgets.
selected.reuse_idea: Prototype a bounded single-voice model, cap solver work and measure worst-case callback time before adding polyphony.
selected.meaningful_repeat_evidence: 23059f69 changes the CA-72 worker wait from 75% to 100% of a block period. This changes real-time audio behavior: late voices can cause a glitch instead of being muted; it is not evidence of improved MCU timing.

selected.description: Free, open source visual audio router for Windows 11. Route, process and record your audio on a canvas: noise gate, EQ, compressor, VST plugins, per-app capture, two-PC streaming, Stream Deck, API and MCP.
selected.content_summary: The Rust DSP crate contains a fixed-hop pitch shifter and a TD-PSOLA voice path with bounded rings, microfft transforms and fixed latency constants.
selected.portability_summary: The small DSP crate is separable from the Windows router. Port only the pitch core or biquads, arrange state allocation at startup and measure FFT/analysis cost; a no_std target build is unverified.
selected.reuse_idea: Run the 1024-point shifter on fixed 128-frame blocks and compare silence, sine and voiced transitions before attempting a Teensy/Daisy callback.
selected.license_note: Root LICENSE is GPLv3; pitch_shift.rs separately attributes an MIT-licensed upstream component.

selected.content_summary: The Eurorack audio-output wing has populated editable KiCad circuitry and a routed PCB, alongside separate control-output wings and main-board assets.
representative_files: Board Files/Euro Audio Output Wing/Wing Board TRS Eurorack Audio Output.kicad_sch

selected.portability_summary: Direct hardware reference for a Teensy multi-codec system. A Daisy design needs its own clocks, codec/control firmware and signal-level review; the wing is not a standalone DSP kernel.
selected.reuse_idea: Adapt the output conditioning as a separate board, checking gain, headroom, grounding and connector pinout before integrating the codec board.

selected.description: VCO core built around the SSI2130 chip
selected.content_summary: Editable KiCad documents implement an SSI2130 VCO core and through-zero FM conditioning, with a populated routed PCB and construction assets.
selected.portability_summary: High value as an analog hardware companion to Daisy/Teensy control or ADC/DAC experiments, not firmware that can be compiled for those boards.
selected.reuse_idea: Study the through-zero FM conditioning and output-level interfaces for an MCU-controlled analog voice; verify calibration and tracking independently.
selected.license_note: Root license is CC BY 4.0. This is a historical hardware reference, last pushed in 2022; source presence is not a current production or measured-performance claim.

selected.description: Modular software synthesizer and algorithmic composition engine in one graph language. C++/GTK4 desktop, WebAssembly in the browser.
selected.content_summary: grain.cpp implements bounded grain slots, interpolation and deterministic stereo clouds; the granular effect reads a live sample ring and supports freeze.
selected.portability_summary: Extract the C++ grain engine and replace graph/plugin plumbing. These .dsp files are Thinksynth graph syntax, not Faust; the eight-second ring needs an explicit MCU memory plan.
selected.reuse_idea: Build one fixed-capacity granular voice in Daisy SDRAM and retain deterministic seeding to compare host and MCU output.

selected.description: A cross-platform cython wrapper of the faust interpreter with rtaudio.
selected.content_summary: Cython wraps libfaust interpreter factories and compute buffers; concrete interpreter tests and CMake targets support a host prototyping workflow.
selected.portability_summary: Use on the development computer to exercise DSP before exporting generated target code. Python, Cython and interpreter factory allocation are not the MCU payload.
selected.reuse_idea: Create repeatable host input/output fixtures for a Faust kernel and compare them with a separately generated Daisy build.
selected.license_note: Project wrapper code is MIT; its LICENSE explicitly preserves separate terms for wrapped and third-party code. This is distinct host tooling adjacent to Faust, not another synthesis kernel.

selected.description: A 4-layer programmable PCB board audio platform featuring an ESP32 DSP core, 50Hz Wi-Fi CSI radar, 2x50W TPA3116D2 Class-D amp, hybrid dual-rail power (10A TPS61088 3.7V-to-12V boost & 12–21V DC jack), 3A USB-C fast charging, BMS protection & Cyberpunk Web HUD. This is more than an amp, a complete wireless sound computer.
selected.content_summary: DspEngine.cpp implements biquad EQ and a radix-2 FFT; main.cpp connects A2DP input to processAudioBlock. Editable schematic and populated PCB data accompany PlatformIO firmware.
selected.portability_summary: The scalar EQ is separable; replace ESP32 Bluetooth, I2S, task and web configuration paths. Hardware assembly and callback correctness were not tested.
selected.reuse_idea: Extract one peaking section, verify coefficient and sample-rate behavior with a sine sweep, then move parameter updates outside the audio callback.
selected.license_note: No root license file was found in the current tree. Keep this as an engineering reference; broader reuse permissions remain unverified.

selected.description: All-in-one compressor plugin for macOS (AU, VST3, Standalone): 14 compressor Modes, from clean digital to VCA, FET, opto, vari-mu and diode bridge, sharing one UI whose curves and meters come from the audio code. C++20, JUCE 8.
selected.content_summary: ProgressiveKnee implements a level-dependent gain law with a bounded Newton solve; DualRelease models two release paths; ScFilter separates side-chain shaping.
selected.portability_summary: The staged DSP is distinct from the JUCE editor, but four-lane SIMD wrappers, templates and solver cost need scalar or ARM replacements before an MCU port.
selected.reuse_idea: Start with the feed-forward knee and dual-release envelope; compare static transfer curves and burst recovery before enabling feedback solves.
